messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: SEV 2 — Private VPC cross-region ILB routing errors detected (control plane API errors). Auto-created incident 1783456789. Investigating.

Ash Patel: Picking this up. Seeing 502s and connection drops between europe-west1 -> us-central1 for ILB-backed private endpoints. Impacting ~24 customer instances (private VPCs).

Maya Chen: I'm on GCP support now. Ticket: https://console.cloud.google.com/support/cases/123456789 — GCP reports 'Internal control plane throttling' on ILB route programming.

Ethan R: Night oncall summary: spike started ~1783456600, intermittent route flaps, some healthchecks show BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE. Applied temporary healthcheck cooldowns, no effect.

Ben Lee: Can we failover affected customers to Dedicated/reserved endpoints? Ops: needs customer approval for routing change, but we have a pre-approved fallback for 6 customers.

Maya Chen: GCP suggested reprogramming routes via gcloud patch, but it may be rate-limited. Raised to GCP SE for control plane fix. ETA unknown.

Ash Patel: Quick mitigation plan: 1) Identify customers with multi-region endpoints; 2) Flip traffic to regional umbrella endpoints where available; 3) For those without, enable short TTL DNS failover -> route through hosted NAT. Starting step 1.

Ash Patel: Running this query to enumerate affected services:
```
SELECT service, customer_id, region FROM infra.routes WHERE status='flapping' AND backend='ilb'
```
Got ~24 rows.

Oncall-Infra: Started a canary DNS failover for cust-17 and cust-42 (small traffic). Monitoring.

Customer Success Bot: FYI sent to oncall-cs with template: "We are investigating connectivity issues for private deployments in cross-region traffic. We're actively working with GCP and will update every 30m."

Maya Chen: GCP SE confirmed throttling due to control-plane API quota bug. They're applying a global rollback to the offending change. Patch in progress.

Ash Patel: Handoff -> Ethan is handing over to me for daytime. Ethan, please capture any runbook changes.

Ethan R: Handover notes: actions attempted: healthcheck cooldown, small route reprogram, DNS canary, opened GCP ticket. Logs in #eng-ops/incidents/1783456789. No config drifts.

Ash Patel: /me taking oncall. Notifying customers on page. Starting broader DNS failover for 12 customers now.

Ben Lee: Reminder: enable fallback auth token so logs still flow to observability. Run:
```
redwood ops auth override --scope=telemetry --expires=2h
```

Ash Patel: Observability: traces show increased 502 at LB level, no spikes in backend CPU. So client-to-ilb path issue.

Maya Chen: GCP update: rollback applied at 1783458400, propagation ongoing. They see slow stabilization in routing tables.

Oncall-Infra: Monitoring shows drop in error rate from 12% -> 3% in the canary group. :thumbsup:

Ash Patel: Rolling back DNS failovers for the canary that is stable. Continuing with staged rollback monitoring windows of 10m.

GCP Support: Final status: control plane rate limiter misconfigured. Fix deployed and control plane API quotas restored. Recommend we validate end-to-end and close incident.

Ash Patel: Confirmed end-to-end connectivity restored for all affected customers. No further errors observed for 30m. Declaring incident mitigated. :white_check_mark:

Maya Chen: Opening postmortem ticket and will coordinate customer follow-ups. Postmortem owner: Maya Chen. RCA timeline stubs in doc: https://redwood-internal/docs/incidents/1783456789

Ethan R: Thanks team — handing back to normal ops. Oncall notes appended. Scheduling postmortem meeting 2/3 of team.

incident-bot: Incident 1783456789 status changed to MITIGATED by Ash Patel. Archived alerts suppressed.
